correctness.rationale: The frozen assertion of identical labelled output supports and empty/full basins fails literally. The rook singleton at (0,0) has an output whose complement is a 6-set with three points in row 0; any size-ten Shrikhande output would be complemented by a union of size six which equals a single Shrikhande neighborhood, with at most two points in every row. Also the whole of row 0 maps to empty on the rook graph but to row 2 on Shrikhande. The corrected RESULT.md and VERIFICATION.md distinguish equality of cardinality data from correspondence under separate permutations. Undirected symmetry gives S subset F^2(S), antitonicity gives F^3=F, and therefore recurrence is precisely the image and an orbit basin is the disjoint union of its incoming fibers. The exact p,q identity was verified on all 65,536 inputs and identifies fibers by p and the empty/full basins by q. An independent union-mask enumeration verifies the eight support/fiber types, 29 equal bivariate coefficients, 654 recurrent states in each graph, all short periods, and every orbit and basin total in the repaired table. It also confirms only 366 common labelled outputs and 48,916 common labelled empty/full basin members. A separate maximal-independent-set count verifies the 24 and 48 fixed points; the displayed repairs do not rely on the intersection counts.
residual_risks: The finite calculations exhaust exactly the two specified labelled 16-vertex systems; neither counts for other graphs nor per-input equality on the original labels is asserted.

value.rationale: The graph pair is motivated by a known shared bipartite double; the natural question is what full one-step data retain about recurrence when the two sides are folded back on common labels. The exact basin comparison answers that question more strongly than a selected run: it identifies which recurrent support sizes produce different pairings, quantifies both fixed and periodic attraction, and distinguishes the temporal systems despite one-step map equivalence. The material added value is not the original false labelled-equality assertion or already-known rook spectrum.
residual_risks: This is a finite witness, not a general separation theorem for all graphs with isomorphic bipartite doubles.
